we have found a way to explain some of the puzzling behaviour of roots, and that this behaviour is consistent with a model of root water uptake in which the membranes of the endoderma cells play a key role in the control of water flow.
the membranes of endodermal cells, which are responsible for the regulation of water flow through roots, are also responsible for many of the responses of young plants to the environment.
the Casparian strips in the endodermises of young roots are not just a barrier to the flow of solutes, but are a key component of the control mechanism which regulates the water relations of plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endodermal cells in young roots have a very important role in the water relations of plants.
the Casparian band, which was thought to be just a barrier, is a very important part of the water uptake process.
a simple model of root water uptake can explain many of the observed phenomena, without the need to invoke complex interactions between roots and soil.
